sources.title: China's New Rare Earth and Magnet Restrictions Threaten U.S. Defense Supply Chains
sources.date_evidence: Critical Questions by Gracelin Baskaran Published October 9, 2025
sources.key_claim: China's October 2025 controls apply the foreign direct product rule to rare-earth magnets for the first time, requiring Chinese government approval to export foreign-made magnets containing at least 0.1 percent Chinese-origin heavy rare earths; China holds roughly 70 percent of rare earth mining, 90 percent of separation and processing and 93 percent of magnet manufacturing.
signals_supported: China rare earth and magnet export controls
Government equity stakes and price floors

sources.title: Antimony 2026: Ample supply, strategic demand to guide geopolitical oversight
sources.key_claim: On 9 November 2025 China's Ministry of Commerce suspended export bans on gallium, germanium and antimony to the United States until 27 November 2026, allowing civilian-use exports to resume under case-by-case approval; antimony prices have declined since a July 2025 peak as Southeast Asian smelting capacity expands.

sources.title: Adjusting Imports of Processed Critical Minerals and Their Derivative Products into the United States
sources.key_claim: A Section 232 proclamation finds that imports of processed critical minerals and derivative products threaten national security, directs Commerce and the USTR to negotiate supply agreements with trading partners, and authorises trade-restricting measures and price floors if negotiations fail; the United States was 100 percent net-import reliant for 12 critical minerals as of 2024.
signals_supported: Government equity stakes and price floors

sources.verbatim_quote: Mining a mineral domestically does not safeguard the national security of the United States if the United States remains dependent on a foreign country for the processing of that mineral.

sources.publisher: Center for Strategic and International Studies
sources.title: New Executive Order Ties U.S. Critical Minerals Security to Global Partnerships
sources.date_evidence: Critical Questions by Gracelin Baskaran Published January 15, 2026
sources.key_claim: The January 2026 executive order shifts US minerals strategy toward allied cooperation on processing rather than unilateral self-sufficiency, directing negotiated agreements and contemplating price floors; China produces about 10 percent of global lithium, cobalt and copper but controls an estimated 40 to 90 percent of processing capacity.
signals_supported: Government equity stakes and price floors

sources.title: Strategic projects on critical raw materials gain momentum in second selection round for potential funding and faster permitting
sources.date_evidence: News article 19 January 2026 Directorate-General for Internal Market, Industry, Entrepreneurship and SMEs ... Publication date 19 January 2026
sources.key_claim: The second call for strategic projects under the EU Critical Raw Materials Act drew more than 160 applications (95 from within the EU, 66 from outside); 75 could support the battery value chain and 21 focus on rare earth elements for permanent magnets, building on 47 EU and 13 third-country strategic projects designated in the first round.
signals_supported: Allied buyers' club and G7 production alliance

sources.title: Special report 04/2026: Critical raw materials for the energy transition
sources.date_evidence: On 2 February 2026, the European Court of Auditors published a Special Report 04/2026 assessing EU measures to secure the supply of critical raw materials (CRMs) necessary for the energy transition.
sources.key_claim: EU auditors found the bloc's 2030 critical raw materials targets appear out of reach: lithium, magnesium, gallium and rare earth elements already exceed the 65 percent single-country import threshold at the processing stage, and diversification efforts via trade agreements and partnerships have yet to produce measurable supply-security results.

sources.title: Trump launches $12B critical mineral reserve to curb foreign reliance
sources.key_claim: President Trump signed an executive order on 2 February 2026 creating Project Vault, a USD 12 billion US Strategic Critical Minerals Reserve funded by a USD 10 billion Export-Import Bank loan and USD 2 billion in private financing, structured as an independently governed public-private partnership with initial OEM participation indicated from Clarios, GE Vernova, Western Digital and Boeing.
signals_supported: Government equity stakes and price floors

sources.title: 2026 IEA Ministerial Declaration Supporting the IEA's Work on Critical Minerals Security
sources.date_evidence: The 2026 IEA Ministerial meeting, where the declaration was adopted, took place on 18-19 February 2026 in Paris.
sources.key_claim: At the February 2026 Paris ministerial, IEA member governments adopted a declaration directing the Secretariat to strengthen the Critical Minerals Security Programme across data collection, market monitoring, emergency preparedness and recycling, and to help countries prepare for supply disruptions caused by export restrictions and accelerate diversification projects.
signals_supported: Allied buyers' club and G7 production alliance

sources.title: Canada advocates buyers' alliance to tackle critical minerals supply concentration
sources.date_evidence: Published: Mar 04, 2026 - 10:56 PM Updated: Mar 04, 2026 - 10:57 PM
sources.key_claim: Canada's Energy and Mining Minister Tim Hodgson said a multilateral production alliance or buyers' club, not just price floors, is the best route to address concentrated critical-minerals supply; Canada signed 30 new deals with 12 countries worth a proposed C$12.6 billion, and France, host of the 2026 G7, has taken up the buyers'-club initiative.
signals_supported: Allied buyers' club and G7 production alliance

sources.title: Strengthening Actions Taken to Adjust Imports of Aluminum, Steel, and Copper Into the United States
sources.key_claim: An April 2026 proclamation strengthens Section 232 tariffs on aluminium, steel and copper effective 6 April 2026, applying duties to the full customs value of covered products and derivatives rather than metal content alone; copper was added to the US critical minerals list in 2025.

sources.title: China's New Supply Chain Security Regime - State Council Order No. 834 and Its Implications
sources.date_evidence: China's New Supply Chain Security Regime - State Council Order No. 834 and Its Implications April 2026 | Asia Pacific
sources.key_claim: On 31 March 2026, Premier Li Qiang signed State Council Order No. 834, China's first dedicated administrative regulation on industrial and supply chain security; in eighteen articles it creates investigation procedures, broad countermeasure authority over foreign states and private actors, and compliance obligations on every organisation within Chinese territory.
signals_supported: China rare earth and magnet export controls

sources.title: Critical Minerals Strategy under the Trump Administration: Progress, Contradictions, and the Road Ahead
sources.date_evidence: the Wilson Center article "Critical Minerals Strategy under the Trump Administration" was published on April 8, 2026.
sources.key_claim: Wilson Center analysis maps the Trump administration's critical minerals roadmap, finding real progress on financing, equity stakes and bilateral agreements but also contradictions, including reliance on a small number of national-champion firms and tension between domestic-production and allied-cooperation goals.
signals_supported: Government equity stakes and price floors

sources.publisher: Associated Press via Alaska Public Media
sources.title: Companies join a deep-sea mining rush after Trump executive order, as regulators fast-track permits
sources.key_claim: Following Trump's executive order to create a deep-sea mining industry, at least nine companies are in talks with the US government for access to seabed minerals; NOAA determined on 1 May 2026 that The Metals Company's consolidated application is in full compliance, with a final permit decision expected before the end of the first quarter of 2027.
